Updated read with SLOOS context: The FOMC keeps policy restrictive (4.25–4.50% range, ongoing balance-sheet runoff) while noting “somewhat elevated” inflation and greater two‑sided uncertainty, which on its face is mildly hawkish. However, the April 2025 Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey points to tighter credit conditions and softer loan demand that lean against growth: banks reported weaker demand (notably in CRE), tighter standards/terms (CRE broadly; C&I tightening at other banks while large banks were mostly unchanged), and cited the economic outlook, supervisory actions, and risk tolerance as reasons. Foreign banks also tightened C&I terms. These SLOOS findings imply an additional drag on activity and disinflationary pressure at the margin, reducing the need for further hikes and reinforcing a “hold/tighter‑for‑longer” stance rather than incremental tightening. Coupled with the FSR’s lingering CRE and nonbank vulnerabilities, the overall tone remains slightly hawkish but tempered by credit headwinds.
